name: Crucible Industries Vibro-Rapier VR-2 'Fencer'
description:
A thrusting sword with an extremely narrow blade that incorporates a longitudinal vibration system along its central axis. Unlike wider vibro-blades that use lateral oscillation to enhance cutting, the Fencer's vibration runs tip-to-hilt, creating a micro-hammering effect at the point that allows the blade to penetrate armor through resonance-assisted micro-fracturing rather than brute force.

The VR-2's blade is barely 12 millimeters wide — too narrow to be effective as a cutting weapon — but the longitudinal vibration transforms it into an armor-piercing instrument of surgical precision. The micro-hammering at the tip creates a cascade of hairline fractures in armor material ahead of the blade's advance, effectively pre-breaking whatever it is about to pierce. Against body armor rated for ballistic threats, the Fencer simply ignores the protection.

Crucible designed the weapon for a specific tactical niche: eliminating armored targets in environments where the noise and collateral damage of firearms are unacceptable. Corporate espionage teams, covert entry specialists, and certain medical practitioners who have found alternative applications for the technology have all adopted the VR-2. The weapon requires significant training to use effectively — its narrow blade offers no blocking surface and its exclusively thrusting technique demands precision footwork and timing.
specifications:
blade_length: 90 cm
total_length: 112 cm
blade_width: 12 mm
weight: 0.6 kg
vibration_axis: Longitudinal (tip-to-hilt)
frequency: 28,000 Hz
power_source: Guard-integrated capacitor, 6 hours continuous
blade_material: Carbon-lattice composite
tactical_use: The Fencer is deployed when an armored target must be eliminated silently. The weapon's vibration-assisted penetration defeats personal armor without the sound or energy signature of a firearm. Operators typically target joints in powered armor, gaps in ballistic vests, and areas where cybernetic hardpoints meet biological tissue. The weapon's narrow profile allows it to be concealed in a cane or collapsed umbrella housing, making it popular among operatives who must pass through security screening.
cultural_context: The VR-2 has revived interest in classical fencing techniques in GLMZ's martial community. Training schools that teach European thrusting traditions have seen enrollment increases as the weapon has demonstrated that historical fighting systems have genuine tactical relevance when backed by modern materials science. The resulting 'neo-fencing' movement blends classical form with BCI-enhanced reflexes, producing a fighting style that is both ancient and futuristic.
story_hooks: A Tier 4 executive was killed by a single VR-2 thrust through a supposedly impenetrable personal shield — the blade's resonance frequency was specifically tuned to the shield's harmonic weakness. Someone had detailed technical intelligence on the victim's protection.
A neo-fencing tournament has been infiltrated by an operative using the event as cover for a real assassination — the target is one of the competitors.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deceptively elegant thrusting blade with an almost needle-like silhouette. The rapier presents a refined, aristocratic form that belies its armor-piercing brutality — the blade appears almost gossamer-thin from most angles, widening only marginally near the cross-guard. The guard itself is minimalist and functional rather than ornate.
physical_description.dimensions: Blade length 90 cm, total length 112 cm, blade width only 12 mm at its widest point. Compact enough for concealment in specialized carriers despite its reach.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light at 0.6 kg — barely over half a kilogram — giving it an almost weightless feel in hand despite its rigid carbon-lattice construction. The balance point sits forward of the guard, favoring precision thrusts.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-lattice composite blade — a proprietary woven structure that appears almost crystalline when caught by light. The guard and pommel are reinforced polymer with integrated capacitor housing.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal with a subtle geometric etching pattern running along the blade's flat surfaces — micro-circuitry traces for vibration distribution. The guard features brushed gunmetal accents where vibration actuators interface with the blade.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep charcoal grey blade with silver-grey vibration nodes along the spine. Guard and pommel in matte black with chrome micro-circuitry visible beneath semi-transparent polymer coating.
physical_description.grip_texture: Wrapped in textured non-slip polymer with subtle haptic feedback zones — the grip itself is engineered to transmit vibration harmonics to the user's hand, allowing experienced operators to 'feel' the resonance cascade during penetration.
distinctive_features: Longitudinal vibration nodes visible as small hemispherical actuators running the blade's length
Capacitor housing integrated into the pommel with faint LED status indicator (blue when charged)
Extremely narrow blade profile — appears almost flat from tip-on view
Micro-circuitry tracery etched along blade surface in geometric precision patterns
Guard designed with minimal surface area to avoid catching on armor seams
Faint resonance shimmer visible along blade edge during operation (28 kHz vibration creates subtle optical distortion)
Serial plate on guard reads 'Crucible Industries VR-2 FENCER' with manufacturing date and batch code
Cross-section reveals hollow blade structure for vibration dampening and weight reduction
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Crucible Industries logo (a stylized crucible symbol) stamped on the pommel. 'VR-2 FENCER' designation etched in small caps along the fuller. BioInk 3D Printing secondary mark near the guard indicates additive manufacturing origin.
physical_description.condition_typical: Corporate-maintained examples appear pristine with perfect edge geometry and flawless polymer finish. Field-used variants show micro-scoring on the blade from repeated armor penetration (hairline scratches in the carbon-lattice), slight discoloration of the polymer grip from blood contact, and worn LED indicators. Some operatives customize their grips with additional wrapping or adhesive coating for specialized glove compatibility.
